title: Getting started with panelviz
text: simulate 120 employees observed weekly half year, weeks missing panel unbalanced — common case practice. as_panel() declares individual time column. recognises time format, sorts data reports shape panel: header tells many individuals periods , whether panel balanced, many rows read. source given printed footer every chart drawn panel.
code: library(panelviz)  set.seed(42) people <- data.frame(   person = sprintf("p%03d", 1:120),   team = sample(     c("Sales", "Operations", "Finance", "Support", "Technology"),     120, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.30, 0.25, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15)   ) ) grid <- expand.grid(   person = people$person,   week = 0:25,   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) grid$week <- as.Date("2024-01-01") + grid$week * 7  d <- merge(grid, people, by = "person") d <- d[stats::runif(nrow(d)) > 0.08, ]           # drop some weeks: unbalanced d$score <- 55 +   as.numeric(factor(d$team)) * 2 +               # teams differ in level   0.2 * as.numeric(d$week - as.Date("2024-01-01")) / 7 +  # slow upward trend   stats::rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 5)                    # individual noise panel <- as_panel(d, id = person, time = week, source = "Simulated data") panel #> # A tidy panel: 120 individuals x 26 periods (week), 2024-01-01 to 2024-06-24 #> # id = person | time = week | unbalanced (92% of id-period cells filled) | 2,862 obs #> # A tibble: 2,862 × 6 #>    .id   .time      person week       team    score #>  * <chr> <date>     <chr>  <date>     <chr>   <dbl> #>  1 p001  2024-01-01 p001   2024-01-01 Support  63.4 #>  2 p001  2024-01-08 p001   2024-01-08 Support  64.3 #>  3 p001  2024-01-15 p001   2024-01-15 Support  71.1 #>  4 p001  2024-01-22 p001   2024-01-22 Support  61.3 #>  5 p001  2024-01-29 p001   2024-01-29 Support  69.9 #>  6 p001  2024-02-05 p001   2024-02-05 Support  60.6 #>  7 p001  2024-02-12 p001   2024-02-12 Support  60.7 #>  8 p001  2024-02-19 p001   2024-02-19 Support  72.6 #>  9 p001  2024-02-26 p001   2024-02-26 Support  67.8 #> 10 p001  2024-03-04 p001   2024-03-04 Support  65.8 #> # ℹ 2,852 more rows

title: Import, Aggregate and Visualise Any Panel Data
text: panelviz R package visualising panel (longitudinal) data. Given column identifies individual column records time, recognises time format, aggregates data time across individuals, draws publication-ready charts. provides consistent set functions stage: read_panel(), as_panel() as_panel_wide() declare data frame, file URL panel (csv, tsv, Stata, SPSS, rds). panel_aggregate() aggregates two stages: within individual time, across individuals group. panel_line(), panel_heatmap(), panel_spaghetti(), panel_tracking(), panel_band(), panel_bar(), panel_stacked() panel_distribution() draw data. share arguments. panel_figure() save_panel() compose numbered multi-panel figures save chart. panel_styles() use_panel_style() select one five looks: economist (default), ft, clean, dark mono.
code: library(panelviz) nls <- read_panel("https://www.stata-press.com/data/r18/nlswork.dta", id = idcode, time = year)  nls #> # A tidy panel: 4,711 individuals x 15 periods (year), 1968-01-01 to 1988-01-01 #> # id = idcode | time = year | unbalanced (40% of id-period cells filled) | 28,534 obs  panel_line(nls, "ln_wage", by = "race")

title: Import, Aggregate and Visualise Any Panel Data
text: Panel data consists repeated observations individuals time, stored long format one row per individual time point. arises economics business (firms, households, markets), public health epidemiology (patients, clinic visits, countries), education psychology (pupils, terms, study sessions), tourism retail (regions, stores, quarters) organisational analytics (employees, weeks). Terminology differs discipline: panel data economics, longitudinal data repeated measures medicine psychology, time-series cross-section political science, grouped hierarchical time series forecasting. individual may called subject, unit, entity participant, time wave, occasion, visit period. Analysing data involves recurring sequence steps: identifying individual time variables parsing time format, aggregating time within individual, aggregating across individuals groups, presenting result form suitable publication. Errors tend arise aggregation steps, example summing stock variable last value meant, reporting statistic group small meaningful. panelviz implements sequence behind single declaration individual time variables. originates plotting functions wpa vivainsights, developed weekly Viva Insights person-level data, generalises panel.

Time collapsed within individual first (fun_time: sum flows, last stocks), individuals collapsed groups (fun_group: mean, median, p90 function). min_n suppresses groups individuals, chart footer reports . Every chart takes arguments. , period, fun_time, fun_group, min_n, tag, source, style return = "table" meaning function. Text derived data. title reports changed, group leads overtook another; subtitle states calculated; Stata variable labels used names. can overridden title subtitle. Axes select units (950, 1.2K, 6M), detect percentages, show year changes. Fonts degrade gracefully. best available condensed typeface used (panel_font()); device render redraws default font.

title: panelviz 1.0.0
text: First release. Release preparation: Reject empty panels missing composite identifiers, keep composite identifiers distinct values contain separators. Support period = "" panels plain numeric time indices. Place line labels group’s last observed value, including groups missing values. Preserve caller’s random-number state sampling individual trajectories. Validate figure dimensions use supported PDF PostScript fonts drawing. Wrap figure headlines subtitles available column width reserve space numbered tags. Keep direct line labels inside panel measuring drawn label positions widening x-axis expansion fit . Lay figure legend keys compact rows shrink type cells keep readable plot area. Add getting-started vignette (vignette("getting-started", "panelviz")) covering full workflow simulated data. Declare panel as_panel(), as_panel_wide() read_panel() (csv, tsv, Stata, SPSS, rds; path URL): say column individual time. Time formats detected: dates, hourly timestamps, years, two-digit years, quarters, months, ISO weeks, yyyymm, text dates, Stata %tm/%tq/%ty plain indices. Ambiguous dates repeated id-time rows stop message. panel_aggregate() aggregates two stages, within individual time (fun_time) across individuals groups (fun_group), min_n privacy floor. Charts: panel_line(), panel_heatmap(), panel_spaghetti(), panel_tracking(), panel_band(), panel_bar(), panel_stacked(), panel_distribution(), panel_plot() choose name. share , period, fun_time, fun_group, min_n, tag, source, style return = "table". Axes pick units detect percentages; titles subtitles computed data can overridden. Five looks: economist (default), ft, clean, dark mono, set use_panel_style() per chart style =. panel_figure() composes numbered multi-panel figures shared source footer; save_panel() saves chart. Charts fall back device’s default font use preferred one.
